entries.name: VA loans
entries.definition: Mortgage loans guaranteed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs for eligible service members and veterans.

entries.name: Data validation
entries.definition: Checking data constraints, populations and transformations.

entries.name: Validation protocols
entries.definition: Writing and carrying out the documented test plans, such as installation, operational and performance qualification, that show equipment, systems or processes work as intended in regulated industries.

entries.name: Valuation of options
entries.definition: Estimating the fair value of option contracts using models such as Black-Scholes or binomial trees.

entries.name: Value proposition
entries.definition: Stating clearly the specific benefits a product or service offers a target customer and why it is better than the alternatives.

entries.name: Value stream analysis
entries.definition: Studying each step of a process that turns inputs into a product or service to find which steps add value and which are waste.

entries.name: Variable-frequency drive
entries.definition: An electronic controller that changes the speed of an AC electric motor by varying the frequency and voltage of its power supply.

entries.name: Variance analysis
entries.definition: Comparing actual results with budgeted or expected figures and explaining the differences.

entries.name: Varnish Cache
entries.definition: An open-source HTTP reverse proxy that caches web content in memory to speed up delivery.

entries.name: VAX 4000
entries.definition: A series of midrange server computers from Digital Equipment Corporation built on the VAX architecture.

entries.name: VAX 8000
entries.definition: A series of high-end computers from Digital Equipment Corporation built on the VAX architecture.

entries.name: VAXELN
entries.definition: A real-time operating system toolkit from Digital Equipment Corporation for building embedded applications on VAX computers.

entries.name: Vector search
entries.definition: Retrieving items using vector representations and a similarity measure.

entries.name: VectorWise
entries.definition: A column-oriented analytical database management system, sold by Ingres and later Actian, which was later renamed Actian Vector.

entries.name: Veeva
entries.definition: A suite of cloud software for the life-sciences industry, covering customer relationship management, content and quality management and clinical operations, made by Veeva Systems.

entries.name: Vehicle inspection
entries.definition: Checking a vehicle's condition, such as its brakes, tires, lights and fluids, for safety and legal compliance.

entries.name: Vehicle maintenance
entries.definition: Servicing and repairing vehicles on a regular schedule to keep them safe and working.

entries.name: Vendavo
entries.definition: Business-to-business pricing and margin management software used to set, optimise and control prices.

entries.name: Vendor management
entries.definition: Selecting, overseeing and evaluating the suppliers a business buys goods and services from.

entries.name: Vendor payments
entries.definition: Processing and issuing payments to suppliers for goods and services received.

entries.name: Ventilator management
entries.definition: Setting up, monitoring and adjusting mechanical ventilators that support or replace a patient's breathing.

entries.name: Verbal and physical intervention
entries.definition: Using de-escalation through words and, as a last resort, safe physical holds to manage a person in crisis or at risk of harm.

entries.name: Version control
entries.definition: Recording changes to files over time in a system, such as Git or Subversion, so that earlier versions can be recovered and several people can work on the same files.

entries.name: Vestibular rehabilitation
entries.definition: Exercise-based therapy that helps people with inner-ear or balance disorders reduce dizziness and improve balance.

entries.name: Video advertising
entries.definition: Creating and running advertisements delivered as video, for example on YouTube, social media and connected TV.

entries.name: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery
entries.definition: Minimally invasive chest surgery performed through small incisions using a camera and long instruments.

entries.name: Video.js
entries.definition: An open-source JavaScript library and player for playing HTML5 video in web pages.

entries.name: Video marketing
entries.definition: Using video content to promote a product, service or brand and to engage an audience.

entries.name: Video remote interpreting
entries.definition: Interpreting between spoken or signed languages over a live video link instead of in person.

entries.name: Videoconferencing
entries.definition: Holding meetings between people in different places by live video and audio, using software or room systems.

entries.name: Virtual design and construction
entries.definition: Using connected digital models of a building's design, schedule and cost to plan and manage a construction project before it is built.

entries.name: Virtual health
entries.definition: Delivering health care at a distance through video, phone, messaging and remote monitoring.

entries.name: Virtual LAN
entries.definition: A way of dividing one physical network into separate logical networks so that devices are grouped regardless of where they are connected, standardised as IEEE 802.1Q.

entries.name: Virtual private network
entries.definition: A technology that creates an encrypted connection over a public network so users or sites can reach a private network securely.

entries.name: Virtual production
entries.definition: Filmmaking that combines live action with real-time computer graphics, often shot in front of LED walls driven by a game engine.

entries.name: Virtual reality
entries.definition: Computer technology that places a user inside a simulated three-dimensional environment, usually through a headset.

entries.name: Virus culture
entries.definition: Growing viruses in living host cells, such as cultured cell lines, to isolate, identify or study them.

entries.name: VISI
entries.definition: A CAD/CAM software package for designing and machining plastic injection moulds, press tools and dies.

entries.name: VisiCalc
entries.definition: An early spreadsheet program for personal computers, first released in 1979.

entries.name: Visier
entries.definition: A cloud people-analytics platform for analysing workforce data such as headcount, turnover and hiring.
